note: Two loops beside freshwater Oceano Lagoon at the north edge of Oceano: sites 1-42 have water and electric hookups, 43-82 none. A trail crosses the park's dunes to the beach, about 400 m. Trailers to 31 ft. The park's $10 dump station is at North Beach Campground, about 3 km north. --Claude
summary: parks.ca.gov page + campground map PDF + ReserveCalifornia (place, both facility grids, unit details, 4 nights priced) + imagery/3DEP read. 82 sites (34+33 web units), 30A + water on 1-42, no sewer; $25-35 campsites, $40-50 hookups; max stay 15; open all year; dump is at North Beach, not here (dump true -> false). WATERFRONT: lakefront not supported (shrub/tree belt on the lagoon shore, loop road between the south row and the water) - coastal walk recommended, lakeview the alternative. Phone 805-489-1869 -> 805-473-7220. Pin is at the Pier Ave entrance ~120 m south of the hookup loop - kept.
flags: WATERFRONT RE-AUDIT (lakefront -> coastal walk recommended; lakeview if AWH prefers to keep it on the lagoon; result does not change it): Oceano Lagoon is a ~50 m-wide freshwater lagoon. South loop (sites 1-42): the east row (odd sites 1-17, ~35.1072-35.1077,-120.6269) sits INSIDE the loop road; at the north end (sites ~13-17, 35.10767,-120.62692) the pads are ~30 m from the water across the loop road, a lawn apron and the Lagoon Trail, then a 5-20 m shrub/tree belt along the shore; farther south (sites 1-11) a dense tree clump and a ~15 m shoreline tree band (to ~-120.6263) stand between. North loop (sites 43-82): the east spurs (51, 53, 56, 57 and 79-82, ~35.1095-35.1100,-120.6263) are ~15-25 m from the water across the trail and a thin but continuous shoreline tree line. 3DEP: pads ~3.8 m, lagoon ~2.4 m, so the bank is gentle, but under the doc a thin tree line or the campground's own loop road means a view at best, and the stored evidence's 'open unused tan sand/grass apron' ends at a shrub belt. Ocean: the dry beach is ~310 m west of the south loop (surf ~450 m) by the Beach Trail across the park's own dunes, with no highway, town or day-use complex on that route (Highway 1 is east of the lagoon; the town is south of Pier Ave) -> coastal walk qualifies. Suggested evidence: 'Esri+3DEP 2026-11-27: Oceano Lagoon (~50 m wide) shore lined by a shrub/tree belt along both loops; south-loop east row inside the loop road ~30 m from water; north-loop east spurs 15-25 m behind a thin continuous tree line -> no on-water; Beach Trail ~400 m across the park dunes to the ocean beach, no highway/town between -> coastal walk.'
